newsitem.title: USA: Hollywood dances with Oscar following nominations.
newsitem.headline: Hollywood dances with Oscar following nominations.

text.p: The Hollywood machine was in high gear on Wednesday, engaging in its annual dance with members of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences following the announcement of the Oscar nominations.
Thousands of videotapes featuring nominated films, artists, directors and screenwriters, will be sent out over the next few days to the 5,000-plus Academy members.
In addition, the nominations, announced on Tuesday, will be trumpeted in newspaper advertisements as well as in movie industry trade papers.

Dick Delson, a Hollywood publicist and an Academy member, said the courtship between the studios and the Oscar voters sometimes starts before the nominations are announced, with studios sending out videotapes of their movies which they believe stand a good chance of being nominated.
"Studios pretty much know when they've got a potential Oscar product, but sometimes even they are taken by surprise," Delson said.

"For instance, I've already received some videos, but I haven't got 'Breaking the Waves' from October Films, presumably because they didn't anticipate Emily Watson being nominated for best actress. No doubt I'll getting that video soon," he added.

Academy members also get videos containing snippets of movies from studios whose products are up for relatively minor awards such as best makeup, best sound, best visual effects and best costume design.
Four of the five movies nominated for best picture are from independent studios, and that could have an impact on the size of the advertising blitz, Delson said.
"The independents simply don't have the money that the big studios can draw on to advertise their nominees," he explained.

The only best picture nominee from a major studio is "Jerry Maguire," from Sony's TriStar Pictures. It also brought a best actor nod for Tom Cruise and a best supporting actor nomination for Cuba Gooding Jr among its five nominations.

Miramax, which produced the 12-nomination-winning "The English Patient," is technically an independent studio, but it has the financial clout of the Walt Disney Co. behind it, having been acquired by the entertainment giant in 1993.

"The English Patient" was nominated for best picture and among its other nominees are Ralph Fiennes for best actor, Kristin Scott Thomas for best actress, Juliette Binoche for best supporting actress, best director for Anthony Minghella and best adapted screenplay, again for Minghella.

Tristar and Miramax are expected to outspend the smaller independents; Gramercy, producer of "Fargo," October Films, which made "Secrets & Lies" and "Breaking the Waves," and Fine Line Features, makers of "Shine."

"Fargo" was nominated for best picture and got six other nods including William H. Macy for best supporting actor, Frances McDormand for best actress, best director for Joel Coen and best original screenplay for Joel and Ethan Coen.

"Secrets & Lies" was nominated for best film and had four other nominees; Brenda Blethyn for best actress, Marianne Jean-Baptiste for best supporting actress, best director for Mike Leigh and best original screenplay, also for Leigh.

The other best picture nominee was "Shine," which also garnered nods for Geoffrey Rush as best actor, Armin Mueller-Stahl as best supporting actor, Scott Hicks for best director and Jan Sardi for best original screenplay.
The Oscars will be handed out March 24 at the Los Angeles Shrine Auditorium.
